WHY: Runs all 8 cleanup jobs including the new multi-query (SELECT+DELETE per batch) annotation cleanup 10x more often, multiplying DB load. HOW: Revert to 10 minutes or justify the frequency change separately.

WHAT: The cleanup job ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. WHY: This runs all cleanup jobs (annotations, expired snapshots/versions/images, short URLs, query history) 10× more frequently, multiplying background DB load and lock contention — the opposite of the deadlock mitigation this PR targets — and appears to be a debug leftover unrelated to the described change. HOW: Restore the ticker to `time.Minute * 10`.

The cleanup ticker was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`, a 10x increase in how often the entire cleanup job runs. This job also drives the annotation/tag cleanup path changed in this PR, which now fetches ID batches into memory and emits Error-level logs per batch, so running it every minute substantially increases DB load and log volume with no functional benefit. Unless a 1-minute cadence is explicitly intended, this should stay at 10 minutes (it reads like a leftover from testing).

issues.descricao: The 'running the max count delete again' test case no longer runs cleanup a second time after the PR's per-subtest seeding and cleanup, so it does not verify that a repeated max-count cleanup deletes nothing.
The annotation cleanup loop stops on a batch whose IDs were already deleted by a concurrent cleaner, leaving the remaining work to the next cycle; checking the fetched count instead would avoid that.
MaxCount annotation cleanup reads victim IDs with LIMIT/OFFSET and deletes them in a separate non-atomic statement, so concurrent deletions can make it delete annotations that should be retained.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The reader thread in the new test catches only Exception, so any Error (e.g., AssertionError, OutOfMemoryError) thrown during concurrent group reads is silently swallowed. WHY: The main thread then asserts caughtExceptions is empty and passes even though the reader thread failed, masking real failures and making the test give false confidence. HOW: Change the catch to Throwable, keep the exception list typed as Throwable, and use assertTrue(caughtThrowables.isEmpty(), ...) so any failure fails the test visibly.

WHAT: The test starts a background reader thread but never joins it before returning. WHY: The reader can continue executing groups() calls after the test method ends, during test cleanup or while the next test is running, causing potential flakiness and cross-test interference. HOW: Join the reader thread after setting deletedAll=true, with a reasonable timeout, and fail the test if it does not terminate.

The reader thread is not joined before asserting caughtExceptions is empty, so exceptions caught after the assertion runs are missed and the test can falsely pass. Store the Thread reference and call thread.join() after deletedAll.set(true) before the assertThat check.

The test starts a reader thread but discards the Thread reference and never calls join(). After deletedAll.set(true) the main thread immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty, so the assertion may run before the reader thread records its final exception. The thread can also continue executing after the test method returns, potentially interfering with subsequent tests or cleanup. Capture the Thread and call thread.join() (handling InterruptedException) after deletedAll.set(true) and before the assertion.

getSubGroupsCount() changed from fail-fast to nullable when the underlying group is concurrently removed. Existing callers that unbox or dereference the result (e.g. long count = group.getSubGroupsCount()) will now throw NullPointerException instead of receiving a count. Either return a safe default such as 0L, or audit and update every consumer to handle null.

getSubGroupsStream (lines 262, 268) still calls modelSupplier.get().method() without null checks. This pre-existing null-safety gap is not modified by this PR and is out of scope for the cross-file analysis.

issues.descricao: The cached GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount returns null when the group was deleted concurrently, violating the GroupModel contract that it never returns null and risking NPEs in callers that unbox it.
issues.textoGolden: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `getSubGroupsCount()` now returns `null` when the delegate model is gone, violating the `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` contract whose javadoc (GroupModel.java:296) states 'Never returns null'. WHY: In-repo callers happen to tolerate a Long null, but any caller that unboxes the result (`long c = group.getSubGroupsCount()`) or does arithmetic on it will NPE, converting the old NPE into a different one. HOW: return a non-null sentinel such as `0L` (and assert the empty/absent case explicitly), or update the interface contract to document a nullable return.

getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the cached delegate is gone (modelSupplier.get() == null), whereas before this change the method delegate-called getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount(), which could not yield null (a missing delegate surfaced as an exception instead). The declared type Long is now genuinely nullable in a path that previously always produced a value or threw, so any caller that relies on the old contract — unboxing the result (e.g. `group.getSubGroupsCount() > 0`, `long n = group.getSubGroupsCount()`, or passing it to a primitive-typed parameter) — will now throw a NullPointerException instead of getting a value or the previous exception. Since consumers were not updated for the new nullable contract, either keep the non-null behavior for callers that cannot handle null or audit/update every caller of GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() to null-check before use.

getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when modelSupplier.get() is null, but the count is consumed as a number by brief-representation building; the sibling cache entity changed in this PR (CachedGroup) handles the same 'model unavailable' case by returning a non-null default (getRoleMappings returns Collections.emptySet(), and the subGroups/attributes loaders are built with non-null empty defaults). Returning null here breaks that convention and can surface as an unboxing/NPE on the consumer side of the read path. Return a non-null value (e.g., 0) or only null if the GroupModel contract explicitly declares it nullable.

issues.descricao: The concurrency regression test never waits for the reader thread before asserting no exceptions, so it can pass even when the concurrent-deletion NPE still occurs.
issues.textoGolden: The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

comentarios.texto: The reader thread is started but never synchronized with: the test does not wait for it to complete a read before deleting, and does not join it before asserting caughtExceptions is empty. The deletes can finish before the reader reads at all, or a failing read can land after the assertion, so the test passes even with the bug present. Use a CountDownLatch counted down after the reader's first successful read, start deleting only after it fires, and join the thread (after setting deletedAll) before asserting.

WHAT: The reader thread started at line 139-149 is never joined before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` runs. WHY: The reader can be mid-request when `deletedAll.set(true)` executes; if that request throws (e.g., reading a group deleted concurrently), the exception is appended to `caughtExceptions` AFTER the assertion has already evaluated, so the test can pass even when the NPE regression it targets is present (and is flaky). HOW: after `deletedAll.set(true)`, `thread.join(<timeout>)` (storing the Thread reference) before the assertion.

The reader Thread is started but never joined, so the assertion at line 157 can execute before the reader has completed a single groups() read (or while a read that would throw the NPE is still in flight). If the GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount null-model NullPointerException were reintroduced, this test could still pass because caughtExceptions is asserted empty before the racing reader thread has recorded anything. Capture the Thread, then join it (e.g. Thread reader = new Thread(...); reader.start(); ... deletions ...; deletedAll.set(true); reader.join();) before asserting so the test actually waits on the condition it verifies.

issues.descricao: The reader thread's stop flag is set only after all deletions succeed, so a failing delete leaves a non-daemon thread polling indefinitely.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The reader loop `while (!deletedAll.get())` has no termination guarantee and `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155 only runs after the delete loop at 152-154 completes. WHY: If any `group(groupUuid).remove()` throws, `deletedAll` is never set, so the non-daemon thread loops forever and the test JVM hangs. HOW: set the thread as daemon and/or wrap deletion in try/finally so `deletedAll.set(true)` always executes.
The test has a mid-loop abort hazard.

The reader's stop flag is set only after every deletion succeeds, with no finally block. If any remove() throws, the test exits with a live non-daemon thread that keeps issuing requests and collecting exceptions indefinitely, interfering with teardown and potentially preventing JVM termination. Put stop signaling and reader termination in a finally block around deletion.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `_is_error_focused_query` decides a query is error-focused by checking if the raw query string contains the substring `event.type:error`. WHY: A negated query such as `!event.type:error` or `NOT event.type:error` still contains that substring, so the function returns True and applies error upsampling to a non-error query, inflating counts. Mixed queries like `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` are also treated as error-only. HOW: Parse the query conditions and return True only when an affirmative `event.type:error` filter is present, or use the existing query parser/AST instead of substring matching.

The truthiness check `if client_sample_rate:` treats a legitimate `0.0` sample rate as missing and silently skips setting `normalized_data["sample_rate"]`. A client sample rate of `0.0` is a valid boundary value meaning "sample nothing / record everything at the client", so it should be propagated explicitly. Replace the truthiness check with an explicit `is not None` (and ideally also validate it is a number, not e.g. an empty string) before converting to float.

The comments on lines 3626-3627 say 'First bucket has 1 event' and 'Second bucket has 1 event', but the assertions on the same lines check that the count equals 10. The count is 10 because the single stored event has client_sample_rate=0.1 and upsampling multiplies by 1/0.1. The comments describe the raw stored events, while the assertions check the upsampled metric value, so the comments disagree with the code they annotate. Update the comments to explain that the bucket contains 1 event that is upsampled to a count of 10, or remove the stale comment.

The `_is_error_focused_query` check does `if "event.type:error" in query`, so any query containing that literal substring is treated as error-focused. This means negations like `!event.type:error`, wildcard terms like `event.type:error*`, or quoted strings like `title:"event.type:error"` can cause `count()` to be rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` for non-error data. The condition should parse the `event.type` predicate or at least require a whole-token match so upsampling is only applied to genuine error queries.

`_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` converts `client_sample_rate` with `float(...)` inside a bare `except Exception`, so values like `"nan"` or `"inf"` become `float('nan')` / `float('inf')` without raising. These non-finite floats are then stored in `normalized_data["sample_rate"]` and can break JSON/queue serialization or produce nonsensical weights. Validate that the converted value is finite and within a sensible range (e.g. 0 < rate <= 1) before storing it.

`_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns `True` for the `errors` dataset, so `count()` is rewritten to `upsampled_count()`. The visible diff only adds the `upsampled_count` SnQL function in `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`; if the errors dataset config does not inherit it, an errors-dataset `count()` query on allowlisted projects will fail with an unknown function error. Either add the function to the errors dataset config or restrict the rewrite to datasets where the function is known to exist.

issues.descricao: The upsampling decision is evaluated against the request's dataset instead of the scoped_dataset actually queried, so in the dashboard discover-split path (metrics dataset) error queries run against discover skip upsampling even when all projects are allowlisted.
issues.textoGolden: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.

comentarios.texto: The upsampling decision uses the closure variable `dataset` while the transformed `final_columns` are executed against `scoped_dataset`. In the dashboard-split path `_get_event_stats` is deliberately invoked with a different dataset (e.g. `_get_event_stats(discover, ...)` at lines 351, 365, 406, 423) than the request's `dataset`, so the `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` branch can be evaluated against the wrong dataset and apply/skip `sum(sample_weight)` for a dataset that was never queried. Base the decision on the dataset actually being queried (`scoped_dataset`) so the transform matches the target of the query.

issues.descricao: _is_error_focused_query uses a substring match for `event.type:error` on the request query, so negated or mixed (OR transaction) discover queries are treated as error-only and get the sample_weight sum instead of count().

comentarios.texto: `_is_error_focused_query` decides whether to apply `upsampled_count()` by doing a naive substring search for `event.type:error` in the raw request query. A query that excludes errors (e.g. `!event.type:error`) or the discover-split query `({query}) AND event.type:transaction` still contains the literal `event.type:error`, so the transform is applied to a non-error / transactions query, summing `sample_weight` where it should be a plain `count()` and producing wrong bucket values. It also ignores the actual `query` passed to `_get_event_stats`, so the decision can differ from the query that is really executed. Match on a parsed/negation-aware condition (or pass the resolved query string) instead of a raw substring test.

The substring check treats `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` as error-only queries. For allowlisted projects this rewrites count() to an aggregation over sample_weight even when the Discover query includes transactions, violating the error-only restriction and potentially failing against a transaction-backed query. Determine the event-type restriction from the parsed query rather than the presence of a substring.

Substring matching does not establish that the Discover query selects only errors. For example, `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` both return True here, causing count() to be replaced with the sample-weight aggregation for non-error or mixed results in allowlisted projects. This contradicts the error-only guard and can produce incorrect counts. Parse the query and establish an error-only restriction (including negation and Boolean structure), or conservatively skip transformation when that restriction cannot be proven.

issues.descricao: test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events cannot detect upsampling being applied to transaction queries, because the transaction has no sample_weight and upsampled_count() equals count() for it.

comentarios.texto: test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events would still pass if upsampling were wrongly applied to transaction queries. The transaction event has no sample_weight, and upsampled_count uses ifNull(sample_weight, 1), so the result is still 1 and 0. Give the transaction a non-default sample rate or weight so an upsampled count would differ from a plain count, or assert that the transform was not applied.

test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events cannot falsify over-application of upsampling: the stored transaction has no sample_weight so upsampled_count() (sum(ifNull(sample_weight,1))) returns 1, same as count(). Give the transaction a sample_weight/client_sample_rate that would diverge (e.g. count 10 if upsampled vs 1 if not), or assert via mock that transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling was not called / yAxes were not rewritten.

test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events cannot detect upsampling being wrongly applied to transaction queries. The stored transaction event has no error_sampling context, so sample_weight is null, and upsampled_count = toInt64(sum(ifNull(sample_weight,1))) evaluates to 1 for it — identical to count(). If _should_apply_sample_weight_transform/_is_error_focused_query were broken so that a discover query with event.type:transaction gets upsampled, the assertion count==1 (and 0 in the empty bucket) would still pass. Add an event with a known non-1 sample_weight (or assert the emitted query uses count() and not upsampled_count) so the test actually fails when the transaction exclusion is bypassed.

issues.descricao: The test factory helper's docstring promises a valid client sample rate but it copies any truthy float-convertible value (negative, >1, strings), unlike production validation.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling uses `if client_sample_rate: float(...)` with no type/range check, unlike production _derive_client_error_sampling_rate which requires isinstance(int,float) and 0<rate<=1. WHY: string '0.1', bool True, or out-of-range 5.0 get stored as sample_rate in fixtures while production drops them, making upsampling tests diverge from prod. HOW: mirror production validation before assigning sample_rate.

The new docstring says the client sample rate must be 'present and valid', but the implementation only checks truthiness and float conversion. Negative rates, rates greater than 1, and float-convertible non-finite values are all accepted and written to sample_rate. This falsely tells test authors that this helper enforces sample-rate validity. Either document that it merely copies truthy float-convertible values, or validate the supported sample-rate range and finiteness before setting the field.

issues.descricao: With upsampling active, top-events queries pick and order the top N groups by raw count() (selected_columns/orderby are not transformed) while the plotted series use upsampled_count(), so ranking can disagree with the displayed weighted counts.

comentarios.texto: Only timeseries_columns are upsampled while selected_columns and orderby used to select the Top N remain based on raw count(). discover.top_events_timeseries first queries those unchanged selected columns to choose groups, so a group with fewer retained events but a higher weighted count is omitted in favor of a lower-volume group. Apply the weighted-count transformation consistently to Top N selection and its ordering as well as the displayed timeseries.

issues.descricao: _are_all_projects_error_upsampled and its caller take an organization argument that is never read.

comentarios.texto: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` takes an `organization` argument — also threaded in from the public `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` — but never reads it: the body uses only `project_ids` and the global option `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`. The declared parameter is dead. Either the allowlist check is meant to be organization-scoped (the body must actually consult `organization`) or the parameter should be removed from both functions; as written the signature advertises an organization-scoped decision the implementation never makes.

issues.descricao: Claims only bare count() is rewritten, so aliased count, eps(), epm(), count_unique() etc. stay un-upsampled.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling only rewrites exact bare `count()` and passes everything else through unchanged. WHY: yAxes like `count() as foo`, `eps()`, `epm()`, `count_unique()`, `count_if()` keep raw counts while should_upsample is true, returning under-counted timeseries. HOW: parse/normalize the function (strip alias, match function name with args) and rewrite all count-equivalent aggs or explicitly fall back to no-upsampling.

issues.descricao: Rewriting count() to `upsampled_count() as count` breaks responses for transformAliasToInputFormat=1: the result column is translated to the rewritten field string while the serializer still reads `count()`.

comentarios.texto: Replacing count() with `upsampled_count() as count` breaks requests using transformAliasToInputFormat=1. QueryBuilder.process_results translates the count alias to the replacement field string, but the endpoint serializer still resolves the original axis as `count()`, so it cannot read the weighted count from the returned rows. Preserve the original public field name in the result mapping when rewriting the internal aggregation.

issues.descricao: upsampled_count truncates the weighted sum with toInt64 instead of rounding, under-counting the estimate by up to one per bucket.

comentarios.texto: `upsampled_count` wraps the sum in `toInt64`, which truncates toward zero: `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))` of e.g. 1.5 or 3.33 yields 1 or 3 instead of the nearest integer, systematically under-counting the upsampled estimate (worst when weights are just below an integer). Use a rounding aggregation (e.g. `toInt64(round(sum(...)))`) so the reconstructed count reflects the intended estimate rather than a floored value.

issues.descricao: The 'no project IDs' test case runs with an empty allowlist mock, so it passes via the empty-allowlist branch and does not verify the empty project_ids guard.

comentarios.texto: The 'no project IDs provided' case does not exercise the `if not project_ids: return False` guard. mock_options.get.return_value was set to [] just above (line 48), so removing the project_ids guard still returns False via the `if not allowlist` branch, and this assertion passes either way. Re-mock options.get to return a non-empty allowlist (e.g. self.project_ids) before calling with project_ids=[], so the empty-project guard is actually falsifiable.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The write lock is held while performing blocking file I/O or an HTTP request to the CDN. WHY: Every concurrent request that needs web assets is serialized behind that single I/O operation, causing a startup/request-time bottleneck. HOW: Perform the asset loading outside the lock and only acquire the lock to read or update the cache pointer; alternatively use sync.Once for initial population and an atomic pointer for reads.

WHAT: After acquiring the write lock, the function does not re-check whether another goroutine already populated the cache, and it assigns `result` to the cache even when `result` is nil due to an error. WHY: A later goroutine that failed to load assets can overwrite a previously successful cache entry with nil, causing every subsequent non-Dev request to re-read the manifest and defeating the cache. HOW: Add a double-checked read after acquiring the write lock and only update the cache when the load succeeded.

The double-check pattern is missing after taking the write lock. This is an internal concurrency/performance issue (not a contract change visible to callers): after acquiring the write lock, the cache should be re-checked before reading the manifest and populating it, to avoid redundant work under concurrent access.

After acquiring entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock(), GetWebAssets should re-check whether entryPointAssetsCache is already non-nil (and cfg.Env != setting.Dev) before reading the manifest again. Without that second check, multiple goroutines that both passed the initial read-locked nil check will perform the file/CDN read sequentially and overwrite the cache, causing duplicate work and possible inconsistent cached values. Add a guarded re-check immediately after the Lock().

issues.descricao: GetWebAssets does not re-check the cache after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent callers that missed the cache each reload the assets manifest.
issues.textoGolden: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The exclusive lock acquired at line 48 is held (via defer on line 49) across the blocking file read / synchronous CDN HTTP request (lines 56-67) and there is no re-check of entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the lock. WHY: On a cold cache, all concurrent callers (api/index.go:82, api/frontendsettings.go:62, middleware/recovery.go:141) block on the write lock and then each sequentially re-executes the full load (file I/O or blocking http.DefaultClient.Do), producing a thundering-herd serialization and N redundant loads instead of one; in Dev mode this happens on every request since the fast path is skipped, serializing all concurrent page loads. HOW: after `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` re-check the cache (`if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`) so only the first goroutine performs the load, and drop the defer in favor of releasing the lock immediately after assigning `entryPointAssetsCache = result` to avoid holding it during I/O.
cache is not re-checked under the lock after re-acquiring write Lock, so concurrent callers can each recompute web assets

The cache is not rechecked after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent production requests that initially observe a nil cache each reload and decode the manifest even after another request has populated it. During a cold-start request burst, these redundant filesystem reads and JSON decodes execute serially under the global lock, delaying queued page and frontend-settings requests and blocking cache readers while each reload runs. After acquiring the write lock, return the populated cache when cfg.Env != setting.Dev before performing asset loading.

issues.descricao: GetWebAssets holds a global exclusive mutex through the whole manifest load, so in Dev mode, where the cache is bypassed, every request serializes behind it.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: deleteScheduledEmailReminder with immediateDelete=true cancels the SendGrid scheduled send but never deletes the WorkflowReminder row. WHY: When a booking is rescheduled via handleNewBooking.ts, the previous booking's email reminders are cancelled with immediateDelete=true and the booking is kept, so the stale rows remain in the database until their scheduledDate passes; the cron only cleans cancelled=true rows, causing a reminder row leak. HOW: Delete the row after the SendGrid cancel request in the immediateDelete branch.

WHAT: The remindersToCancel loop awaits each SendGrid cancel request sequentially. WHY: Each cancelled reminder within the next hour triggers a separate blocking network round-trip, so cancellation latency grows linearly with the number of cancelled reminders and can delay the cron run. HOW: Collect the client.request promises and await Promise.all, or use a bounded concurrency helper like async.mapLimit.

The function deleteScheduledEmailReminder now, by default, only sets `cancelled: true` on the row and does not delete it, while its name and the callers' expectations (e.g., 'deleteScheduledEmailReminder') say it deletes the reminder. Rename it to something like cancelScheduledEmailReminder or split the 'mark cancelled' and 'delete' paths so the name matches the behavior.

When `referenceId` is present and `immediateDelete` is true, the function cancels the SendGrid batch but returns without deleting the `WorkflowReminder` row or setting `cancelled: true`. Because the cleanup cron only processes rows with `cancelled: true`, these reminders are never removed from the database. For callers that are not followed by a cascade delete (e.g. rescheduling in `handleNewBooking.ts`), this leaks stale rows. The `immediateDelete` branch should either delete the row directly (matching `deleteScheduledSMSReminder`) or mark it `cancelled: true` so the cron can remove it.

issues.descricao: Reminder cancel helpers are called without await inside forEach when bookings are cancelled/rescheduled or workflows edited, so the handler can return before reminders are cancelled or deleted and failures are unobserved.
issues.textoGolden: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder called inside forEach without collecting/awaiting promises. WHY: handler returns before cancels complete and rejections are unobserved, so cancellations are lost and reminder emails/SMS are still sent (same fire-and-forget pattern repeated in handleNewBooking:966, bookings.tsx:488, workflows.tsx:212/376/519/574).

Cancellation now delegates the database update/deletion to asynchronous reminder helpers without awaiting them, while removing reminder deletes from the awaited promise list. The handler can finish before cancelled flags or unscheduled-reminder deletions are persisted, allowing a subsequent scheduler run to schedule a cancelled booking's reminder and leaving cancellation work unfinished when a serverless invocation terminates. Collect and await the helper promises; apply the same correction to the modified rescheduling and workflow-update callers that discard these promises.

Await the reminder cancellation promises before completing the cancellation request. These helpers now own persistence of cancellation: email awaits a workflowReminder update and SMS awaits Twilio before deleting the row. The forEach discards their promises, and removing remindersToDelete from the awaited promise list removes the previous guarantee that reminder state is cleared before the handler returns. In a serverless request the outstanding operations can be interrupted after the response, leaving reminders active for a cancelled booking. Collect these helper promises and include them in the awaited Promise.all.

issues.descricao: The cron cancels SendGrid sends for cancelled reminders in one try around the whole loop, so one failing cancel aborts all remaining cancellations and the row deletions, and the failing row blocks later runs.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: remindersToCancel loop awaits SendGrid cancel per-reminder inside one try and only runs Prisma deletes after the loop, with no method filter. WHY: a single throw (e.g. null SMS referenceId sent as batch_id, or one SendGrid error) aborts the loop and skips Promise.all deletes, leaving all other cancelled emails still scheduled so they are still sent.

Successful cancellation records are only deleted after every SendGrid request in the loop succeeds. If a later request fails, the catch skips all queued Prisma deletions; the next run retries an already-cancelled batch, which SendGrid rejects with 400, and aborts before processing the remaining reminders. Await each reminder's database deletion immediately after its successful cancellation and isolate errors per reminder so one failed batch does not block the others.

Handle cancellation failures per reminder rather than around the entire batch. If one SendGrid request rejects (for example, for an expired or invalid batch ID), the loop exits before cancelling the remaining reminders, and Promise.all is never reached, so even earlier successfully cancelled reminders remain in the database. The failed record stays eligible for the next run and can repeatedly block other cancellations until their emails are sent. Execute each successful deletion and isolate failures so the worker continues processing the remaining reminders.

issues.descricao: Email reminders for cancelled bookings are only flagged cancelled and cancelled in SendGrid by the cron later, so reminders close to their send time can still be delivered.

comentarios.texto: Deferred cancellation includes reminders less than ten minutes from their scheduled send time, when SendGrid no longer permits cancellation. A booking cancelled in that interval is only marked cancelled locally by deleteScheduledEmailReminder, and the cron's POST is rejected, so its email is still delivered. Process cancellation before SendGrid's ten-minute cutoff and explicitly handle cancellations that arrive after that deadline rather than relying on this cron query to stop delivery.

issues.descricao: The cron cancels SendGrid scheduled sends one at a time with sequential awaits, which is slower than batching.

comentarios.texto: The new cancel loop performs a sequentially awaited SendGrid HTTP request (`await client.request(...)`) for each reminder returned by an unbounded `findMany` (no `take`), then deletes them. WHY: this is O(N) serial network round-trips per cron run; if many reminders are cancelled at once (e.g. a bulk event-type disable or booking cancellation wave) the cron handler can block for a long time on serial SendGrid latency. HOW: fan the independent SendGrid cancel requests out with `Promise.all`, and/or bound the query with `take` plus pagination, then batch the DB deletes.

WHAT: SendGrid cancel issued with sequential await inside for loop over remindersToCancel. WHY: cron blocks O(N) sequential network round-trips instead of parallel batch, materially slowing the hourly schedule job as cancelled backlog grows.

issues.descricao: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and its immediateDelete flag do not delete anything; the names no longer describe the behaviour.

comentarios.texto: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and its `immediateDelete` flag no longer match what the code does. The default path only marks the reminder `cancelled: true`, and the `immediateDelete` path only sends a cancel request to the email provider. Neither path deletes the scheduled send or the row, unlike the SMS counterpart, which still deletes. Rename them (for example `cancelScheduledEmailReminder` and `immediateCancel`) or document the behaviour.

issues.descricao: deleteScheduledSMSReminder deletes the DB row only after a successful Twilio cancel, so a cancel failure leaves the reminder row behind now that callers no longer delete it.

comentarios.texto: twilio.cancelSMS and prisma.workflowReminder.delete share one try block. If the Twilio cancel throws, the DB row is never deleted. The reminder row then stays behind for a booking that was cancelled, rescheduled or deleted, because the callers no longer delete rows themselves. Delete the row in a finally block, or handle the cancel failure separately so the delete still runs.

issues.descricao: Prisma is imported in workflows.tsx but no longer used.

comentarios.texto: `Prisma` is imported as a value (line 9) but is no longer used anywhere in this file. This PR removed the only usages (`Prisma.BatchPayload` in the now-deleted `remindersToDelete` / `deleteReminderPromise` declarations), while the import was kept. WHY: the repo's ESLint `no-unused-vars` rule will fail CI/build for an unused import. HOW: remove `Prisma` from the import list (and keep `import type { PrismaPromise }` as a type-only import).

issues.descricao: The cron route sets the API key only on @sendgrid/mail, so the new @sendgrid/client cancellation requests are unauthenticated and reminders for cancelled bookings stay scheduled.

sugestoes.texto: The Javadoc/comment for USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH still describes the previous behavior of preventing user clearing on failed password authentication. After the refactor the flag is consumed only by AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError to hide the username and disable registration during re-authentication. The comment should be updated to match the current observable effect, otherwise future maintainers will look for user-clearing logic that is no longer governed by this flag.

issues.descricao: PasswordForm now accepts passkey-only users, but only the keycloak.v2 login-password.ftl renders the passkeys conditional UI; the base template (used by the legacy keycloak theme) does not, so a passkey-only user is shown a password-only form they cannot complete.

comentarios.texto: PasswordForm.configuredFor now accepts passkey-only users even when the active login theme renders the unchanged base login-password.ftl, which contains no passkeys UI. The legacy keycloak theme inherits that template, so a user without a password reaches a password-only challenge with no way to authenticate instead of being able to use the newly accepted passkey credential. Add the passkeys import and conditionalUIData invocation to the base login-password.ftl as well as the keycloak.v2 override.

issues.descricao: The comment 'setup webauthn data when passkeys enabled' does not mention that the condition also requires a selected user to own a passkey credential.

comentarios.texto: The new comment says webauthn data is set up "when passkeys enabled", but the guard `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` also requires that a known/already-selected user actually has a passkey credential. With realm passkeys enabled and a selected user without a passkey, `fillContextForm` is skipped (the test `passwordLogin_reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` relies on exactly this), so the comment misdescribes the condition it documents. Rephrase it to match the code, e.g. "setup webauthn data when conditional passkeys can be used (user unknown or user has a passkey)".

issues.descricao: The test comment says it sets the passwordless policy for discoverable keys, but the updater only disables passkeys for the realm.

comentarios.texto: The comment 'set passwordless policy for discoverable keys' is stale. The updater now only calls setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE), so it disables passkeys for the realm. Change the comment to say that passkeys are disabled for the realm.
